title: Elastic KV-swapback preemptor with time-decayed fairness ledger
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Continuous batching improves GPU utilization by aggregating requests, but long-lived KV cache residency and aggressive batch accumulation cause asymmetric memory pressure across tenants and can force hard preempts that violate SLOs. Goal: design a preemption and fairness policy that (1) reclaims GPU memory predictably under bursty load, (2) maintains high KV hit rates for latency-sensitive tenants, and (3) imposes bounded tail-latency regressions for SLO-critical traffic. Proposal: implement an Elastic KV-swapback Preemptor that combines three ideas: 1) soft-suspend tokens: track per-tenant soft-suspend credits that permit temporary de-scheduling of low-priority microbatches without evicting their KV working sets immediately; 2) time-decayed fairness ledger: maintain a decaying score per tenant that accrues when they consume GPU time or KV bytes and decays with a tunable half-life, enabling fairness to adapt to changing workloads; 3) KV-swapback: instead of immediate eviction, serialize cold KV shards to a compact swap object in host memory (or NVMe) with quick rehydrate heuristics and per-shard fingerprinting to bound rehydration cost. This hybrid approach trades modest IO for fewer hard preempts and smoother latency tails. Implementation outline: - Scheduler extension: incorporate ledger score and soft-suspend tokens in admission and preempt decisions. - KV manager: add per-shard swapback path + residency state machine (resident | swapped | ghost). - Admission rules: short-circuit low-latency requests (high-priority tag) to skip swapback if KV residency is critical; otherwise allow swapback/soft-suspend for background or bulk requests. - Backpressure integration: hook into continuous-batcher to allow microbatch suspend/resume with QoS hints (max-suspend-duration). - Observability: emit metrics for ledger scores, swapback count, rehydrate latencies, and soft-suspend durations. - Config knobs: ledger half-life, soft-suspend budget per tenant, swapback threshold, rehydrate concurrency. Rationale: Existing preemptors focus on eviction-first or token-bucket fairness which leads to oscillations in KV hit rate and cascaded rehydration cost. Swapback amortizes eviction cost and the decayed ledger handles fairness for bursty tenants without permanently penalizing them. Trade-offs considered: - IO cost vs eviction cost: swapback reduces expensive model re-initializations but uses host I/O; for NVMe-backed nodes this is acceptable and configurable. - Implementation complexity: state machine for KV shards and atomic swapback/rehydrate paths add complexity; mitigated by reusing existing KV eviction code paths where possible. - SLO risk: misconfigured ledger half-life could cause unfairness; default conservative values and canary rollout planned.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Under mixed workload benchmark (40% high-priority low-latency, 60% background bulk) the 99p latency for high-priority requests increases by <8% vs baseline and p95 by <5%. 2) Average KV hit rate degradation <= 3% for latency-critical tenants compared to baseline. 3) The number of hard GPU preempts (forced eviction + immediate restart) reduces >= 40% in stress tests simulating bursty tenants. 4) End-to-end e2e perf test (end-to-end CI) and one canary cluster indicates no regressions in crash rate or OOMs for 72h. 5) Observability: new metrics show ledger distribution and swapback counts; dashboards created in Grafana linked in ticket. 6) Feature toggled behind a runtime flag and rollout plan in place.
implementation_notes: Planned PRs: scheduler changes (github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/2234), kv-swapback manager (github.com/redwood-inference/kv-manager/pull/198), observability hooks (github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/112). Start with unit tests for state transitions, then integration test with microbench harness (see perf/benchmarks/swapback). Key files: scheduler/preemptor.cc, kv/rehydrate_service.cc, telemetry/metrics_def.yaml. Reuse existing kv-eviction metrics and extend them for swapback states.
progress_updates: 2025-01-21: Initial design sketch completed; whiteboard session with infra and kv team. Decided to prefer staged rehydrate over immediate eviction for NVMe-backed hosts.
2025-01-28: Prototype of time-decayed ledger in scheduler simulation harness. Basic fairness properties validated in synthetic traces.
2025-02-10: KV manager swapback prototype implemented; uses blob store API to write compacted shard. Rehydrate latency microbenchmark shows median 1.2ms, p99 12ms for 4KB shards on NVMe instance.

2025-02-24: Integration test with continuous-batcher harness shows 28% reduction in hard preempts but a 6% increase in p99 latency for high-priority throughput; tuning ledger half-life to reduce tail impact.
2025-03-01: Added per-tenant soft-suspend token accounting and admission hook; initial A/B canary scheduled for 2025-03-10 against a small subset of dedicated nodes.
2025-03-05: Observability dashboards added and PRs opened for review (see implementation_notes links).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Swapback IO could saturate host PCIe/NVMe under pathological workloads -> Mitigation: rate-limit rehydrate concurrency and backpressure to batcher, fall back to immediate eviction when IO budget exhausted.
Risk: Ledger misconfiguration leads to starvation -> Mitigation: conservative defaults, tenancy quotas, and emergency kill-switch to disable ledger-based preemption per node.
Risk: Implementation bugs causing KV corruption -> Mitigation: checksum-based shard fingerprinting, integration tests that validate end-to-end correctness, and canary rollout with slow ramp.
alternatives_considered: 1) Immediate eviction with predictive refill: proactively evict and asynchronously refill likely-needed shards. Rejected due to higher rehydration churn and model warmup costs.
2) Strict token-bucket fairness per-tenant without decay: simpler but penalizes bursty tenants permanently and performed worse in fairness simulations.
3) Cross-tenant cooperative caching: shared cold-set index to reduce duplication. Strong but requires global coordination and more infra changes; deferred to future phase.
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger math and token accounting; KV manager unit/integration tests for swapback/rehydrate correctness; perf harness: run mixed workload (T=12h) comparing baseline vs swapback with 10k simulated tenants; canary: enable on 5% of dedicated nodes for 72h and monitor SLO dashboards and OOMs.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal test cluster with runtime flag ON for 1 node (2 weeks). Stage 2: Canary on 5% dedicated clusters (72h, abort on predefined thresholds). Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 50% with monitoring and ops runbook. Stage 4: Global enable if stable.

notes: This ticket targets a pragmatic middle ground between eviction-first preemptors and full global cooperative caching. If successful, follow-ups: (a) tenant-adaptive ledger half-life tuning, (b) ML model to predict rehydrate necessity, (c) NVMe tiering policies for larger shards.
